I was working the door at one of our house parties last semester (my school doesn't have Greek housing. Yay, lawsuits.), and the guy working the door with me was a senior (I was a sophomore) who gave no fucks. Now, I've been told I'm too nice to work the door, which is fairly true, so when my Brother, who we'll call Buddy, can be a pretty big asshole if he wants to. Tonight, however, was not one of those nights.

A bit of backstory: my fraternity is known on campus for throwing pretty awesome parties, so when we throw one, there's usually a good amount of people coming and going throughout the night. The biggest traffic is around midnight when everyone's either done pregaming or one of the other parties has run out of alcohol (a common occurance, unfortunately. Especially this early on for some fraternities). This part of the night happened around then.

We had a big crowd of people outside of our gate to the backyard of the house the party was at, and we had been letting people in we knew first to the point where the crowd inside was getting pretty big. A group of seven people (5 guys, 2 girls) walked up and tried to get in. Early on, this wouldn't be a problem, but since it was getting too big, and we didn't want the guy/girl ratio to go down, we had to turn them away. Naturally, they argue about it, demanding to be let in. As this is going on, a small (about 5'5) guy tunnels his way through the crowd to get to me and flashes a wristband for the Delt party 6 blocks away. The arguing stops as I just stare at him, his eyes wide with anticipation and hope that this ruse might get him the coveted alcohol he desires. I say the words "We aren't fucking Delt," and he immediately turned and hightailed it out of there. The crowd of 7 and I had a good laugh, and I eventually let them in after a few more people left.

The second part comes from about an hour and a half later, about 1:30 AM. I took a break and went back to the door with Buddy and were standing there being bored (the crowds had died down. We had a few party hoppers come and go, but that was it). Buddy was a bit more drunk than I was, but we were having a good time. Everything was quiet until we saw two large shadows approach. Buddy hit them both with a light and saw that it was two morbidly obese girls waddling towards us (these girls were at least 400 lbs each. No joke). Buddy stops them and asks who they know here, etc., etc. Instead of answering any questions, they flash two fifths of rum and say, "We brought alcohol." Bad sign that it was only two fifths of rum, but that didn't deter Buddy from saying "Fuck it, go on in."

The two girls were in there for 15 minutes before getting tossed out, still clutching their same bottles of rum and yelling loudly about how they were being thown out because they weren't white (one was African-American, one was Hispanic). Buddy asked what happened, to which one of our other Brothers, who will be known as Guy, said "Friend (our African-American Brother) caught them chugging glass after glass of the punch inside. About three-fourths of the new batch was finished by them." These are the multiple gallon coolers that they have on the sidelines at sporting events for the players.

The girls continued to protest and yell as we got them out of there (took about 4 of us to do it), but we did. After that the party went on like normal until the cops busted it up at 3 AM.

Good times... Goooood times...

America is not a democracy, and we never were. America is instead a republic, meaning that your contribution ends at casting your vote on a representative who will speak/vote for you.

It even says in the Pledge of Allegiance that we are a Republic, "I pledge allegiance to the Flag of the United States of America, and to the Republic for which it stands, one Nation under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all."

And yet, when I tell people we're not a democracy, they're freaking out over it.

The American people will have the chance to read the TPP before it is passed; it will just be very difficult to prevent its passage because of the lowered standards for passing it (i.e. fast-track). However, we will not be able to see the negotiation documents until four years after the negotiations end. In other words, we won't know what went into the sausage for four years, but we will be able to see the sausage itself right away.
